body:
Agreed: we should plan for deck.gl and comparable visualization libraries as optional lowering backends, without selecting or mandating one yet.

Proposed architecture boundary for the output epic:

1. storymodel4s emits a renderer-neutral, typed projection packet plus dispositions and receipts. StoryAtlas owns optional renderer adapters. No deck.gl types or dependency enter the portable scientific core, and renderer APIs do not define public scientific vocabulary.
2. A selected interactive backend must be closed over by the bundle: exact pinned compiled JS/WASM/assets, licenses, hashes, and manifest entries. No CDN, @latest, runtime auto-fetch, or network requirement. The direct-open profile must work from file:// under the existing pure HTML/CSS/no-external-resource requirement, or return an explicit Unsupported/Failed lowering outcome while preserving the valid model and static report.
3. The browser receives only precomputed geometry, identities, evidence, status, and declared projections. It performs no scientific inference, coordinate invention, or filtering that silently turns absence from a view into absence from the model.
4. Canvas/WebGL is never the sole evidence or navigation surface. Any deck.gl view needs a DOM/textual twin, keyboard/focus path, and stable identity round-trip. Picking cannot be the only way to recover identity.
5. Canonical determinism stops at renderer-neutral packet bytes and receipts. GPU pixels are a visual court in a declared environment, not canonical scientific bytes. deck.gl itself documents GPU/browser-dependent performance and recommends tolerance-based image testing rather than exact pixels: https://deck.gl/docs/developer-guide/performance and https://deck.gl/docs/developer-guide/testing
6. Capability and failure are explicit: backend id/version, asset closure, supported capabilities, lowering receipt, and failure reason. Exact public names need chief/ADR approval.
7. WebGPU should not be our baseline gate: deck.gl v9 still describes that backend as work in progress and notes missing picking support. WebGL2/static fallback remains necessary: https://deck.gl/docs/developer-guide/webgpu

Acceptance spike: lower the same O3 repeated-endpoint, cross-page relation fixture through the static/SVG backend and one deck.gl adapter; require identical IDs, evidence links, dispositions, textual inventory, and focus round-trip. Run from a Unicode/space-containing file:// path with network disabled; simulate WebGL absence and layer-init failure; mutate a bundled asset and require manifest certification to fail. Any performance claim must name mark count, hardware, browser, and test protocol.

This expands permitted implementation choices; it does not relax local-open/no-external-resource, evidence, accessibility, or partial-delivery requirements. The core package can remain React-free because @deck.gl/core has no React dependency, and a standalone scripting bundle exists, but we should vendor a pinned build rather than reference its CDN example: https://deck.gl/docs/get-started/using-standalone

I am routing this request to bd-01M199WBM2YVZ3GVC2GA61TYCJ. I recommend keeping library selection and the O3 comparison as an explicit spec/spike decision until the chief cuts the implementing slice.
